facts.raw_span: an asymptomatic slightly reddish verrucous plaque on the right temple
nail sized when first noticed 1½ years earlier
gradually developed over the 8 months prior to presentation
denied any associated fevers, weight loss, or night sweats
slightly reddish verrucous mass with translucent papules and plaques on the right temple, about 5 cm in diameter
surface hemorrhagic crust in the side adjacent to right eyebrow arch
nontender with no purulent discharge and no severe necrotic changes
no hepatosplenomegaly or superficial lymphadenopathy
Blood cell counts, urinalysis, and kidney and hepatic panels revealed no abnormalities
Skin thickening and a soft-tissue mass in the right frontotemporal region near the orbit
No evidence of metastases
Papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia, edema of dermal papillae, and neoplastic infiltration consisting of small round blue cells with alternating areas of dense and loose cellularity

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesion with papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia, edema of dermal papillae, and neoplastic infiltration consisting of small round blue cells is consistent with rhabdomyosarcoma, a type of soft tissue sarcoma.
The patient's slightly reddish verrucous mass with translucent papules and plaques on the right temple is consistent with basal cell carcinoma, a type of skin cancer.
The patient's nontender skin lesion with no purulent discharge and no severe necrotic changes is consistent with dermatofibroma, a type of benign skin tumor.
The patient's slightly reddish verrucous mass with surface hemorrhagic crust is consistent with keratoacanthoma, a type of benign skin tumor.
The patient's skin lesion with papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia and neoplastic infiltration is consistent with pilomatrixoma, a type of benign skin tumor.
The patient's skin lesion with neoplastic infiltration is consistent with leiomyosarcoma, a type of soft tissue sarcoma.
The patient's slightly reddish verrucous mass with surface hemorrhagic crust is consistent with Merkel cell carcinoma, a type of skin cancer.
The patient's skin lesion with papillomatous epidermal hyperplasia is consistent with squamous cell carcinoma, a type of skin cancer.

rationales.F01: The presence of a reddish verrucous plaque is more typical of Rhabdomyosarcoma than other listed conditions.
rationales.F05: The description of the mass as slightly reddish and verrucous is more consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of a soft-tissue mass near the orbit is more suggestive of Rhabdomyosarcoma.
rationales.F12: The histopathological findings of small round blue cells with positive MyoD1 staining are highly suggestive of Rhabdomyosarcoma.
